annotations.description: With World Breaker and Ruin in Their Wake in hand but no green mana sources, the player needs mana development urgently. Planar Atlas would provide colorless ramp toward World Breaker and its ETB could find a green land to enable Ruin in Their Wake. Shacklegeist provides a 2/2 flyer but doesn't address the fundamental mana problems in this hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Shacklegeist, a 2/2 flyer with limited utility (tap ability needs 2 spirits)
annotations.betterLine: Cast Planar Atlas to start ramping toward World Breaker and use its ETB to dig for a green land, enabling Ruin in Their Wake for further mana development

annotations.description: Cast Fetid Imp without playing the Swamp from hand first. Playing land before casting spells is a fundamental sequencing principle - it costs nothing and keeps options maximally open. With Swamp played first, they'd have 3 mana available, which doesn't change this turn's options but ensures no mana is wasted on future turns.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Fetid Imp using Island + Thriving Moor without first playing the Swamp land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp first, then cast the 2-drop. Additionally, Erratic Visionary may have been the better creature choice here, as card filtering helps dig toward the 6-mana bombs (Ormos, Tolarian Kraken) while being unblockable by Shacklegeist.

annotations.description: Passed on casting Essence Flux on Shacklegeist (a Spirit) which would have returned it with a +1/+1 counter, making it a permanent 3/3 flyer. While holding Essence Flux for protection has value, the proactive use here gives a meaningful permanent upgrade to their only threat for just {U}.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to cast Essence Flux with the Planar Atlas trigger on the stack
annotations.betterLine: Cast Essence Flux targeting Shacklegeist to get a permanent +1/+1 counter (Spirit bonus), upgrading it to a 3/3 flyer. The opponent has minimal board presence and the aggressive upgrade likely outweighs holding for protection.

annotations.description: Activating Fetid Imp's deathtouch before blockers are declared. If the opponent doesn't block (likely since trading Shacklegeist for a 1/2 is debatable), the {B} is wasted. Better to wait until after blockers are declared to decide whether deathtouch is needed.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Fetid Imp's deathtouch ability during the pre-block combat step, spending {B}.
annotations.betterLine: Pass priority before blocks, then activate deathtouch only if Shacklegeist blocks. This preserves the option to spend that {B} on something else or leave mana open.

annotations.description: Opponent's Fetid Imp (1/2 flying) is attacking and opponent has all lands tapped, so deathtouch cannot be activated. Shacklegeist (2/2 flying) can legally block it (Shacklegeist can block flyers) and would kill the Imp while surviving at 2/1. This is a free creature kill with no risk.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to block, taking 1 damage and leaving Fetid Imp alive.
annotations.betterLine: Block Fetid Imp with Shacklegeist to kill it for free, since opponent has no mana to activate deathtouch.

annotations.description: Casting Erratic Visionary over Rousing Read on Fetid Imp. Rousing Read would draw 2 cards (netting +1 card advantage), create a 2/3 flying creature with deathtouch activation, and help dig toward the 4th land needed for Oneirophage. Erratic Visionary is a slower investment that requires additional mana each turn to generate value.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Rousing Read on Fetid Imp for {2}{U}, drawing 2 cards and discarding 1, creating a 2/3 flying deathtoucher that pressures the opponent immediately while providing card advantage.

annotations.description: Activated Fetid Imp's deathtouch ability for {B} when attacking into no possible blockers (Shacklegeist was tapped, Murmuring Phantasm can't block flyers). The deathtouch is completely irrelevant since no creature can block the Imp. While there was nothing else useful to spend the mana on this turn, it's still an unnecessary activation.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with Fetid Imp and activated deathtouch for {B}
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Fetid Imp without activating deathtouch, saving the mana (even though there was likely nothing else to do with it, it's better practice to not waste resources).

annotations.description: Declined to block Fetid Imp (1/2 flying) with Murmuring Phantasm (0/5 defender) when the opponent had all lands tapped, meaning they couldn't activate deathtouch or cast any combat tricks. The block would have been completely free - Phantasm survives with 1 damage marked and no damage gets through.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed on blocking, taking 1 damage from Fetid Imp.
annotations.betterLine: Block Fetid Imp with Murmuring Phantasm for a risk-free block that prevents 1 damage.

annotations.description: Erratic Visionary attacks into Murmuring Phantasm (0/5 defender), dealing 1 irrelevant damage to a 5-toughness wall. This wastes the opportunity to use Erratic Visionary's loot ability ({1}{U}, {T}: draw then discard), which is valuable for finding lands and filtering toward powerful cards like Oneirophage and Tolarian Kraken in hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with both Fetid Imp and Erratic Visionary
annotations.betterLine: Attack with only Fetid Imp (flies over for 1 damage), then use Erratic Visionary's loot ability in second main phase to filter through the deck toward land drops needed for the expensive cards in hand (Tolarian Kraken at 6 mana, Ormos at 6 mana).

annotations.description: Cast Liliana's Standard Bearer with X=0 (no creatures died this turn), completely wasting its powerful ETB card draw ability for just a fragile 3/1 body. The card's main value is its ETB trigger, which drew nothing here.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Liliana's Standard Bearer as a vanilla 3/1 with no card draw.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Oneirophage (3U), which synergizes with Erratic Visionary's draw ability and Rousing Read in hand. It would grow into a significant flying threat over subsequent turns. Alternatively, cast Rousing Read on Erratic Visionary for immediate card advantage (+2 cards drawn, +1/+1 and flying). Save Liliana's Standard Bearer for a turn when creatures actually die (e.g., after a Barter in Blood or combat deaths) to get real card advantage.

annotations.description: Bounced Fetid Imp instead of Erratic Visionary. While Fetid Imp's flying deathtouch threatens GPT53C's flyers, Erratic Visionary is a repeatable card-filtering engine that generates ongoing card advantage. Bouncing the Visionary would deny the opponent their best source of card selection and force them to spend mana replaying it.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Fetid Imp with Roaming Ghostlight's bounce ability
annotations.betterLine: Bounce Erratic Visionary to remove the opponent's card advantage engine and force them to re-invest mana to replay it

annotations.description: Barter in Blood is a symmetric sacrifice effect that costs Haiku Nature 2 of their 3 creatures while the opponent loses 2 of 4. The opponent likely sacrifices their worst creatures (Murmuring Phantasm + one other) and keeps their best threats. Runed Servitor dying also gives the opponent a free card. At 14 life facing flyers, reducing board presence might help, but Haiku Nature ends up with just 1 creature vs opponent's 2 remaining (likely strong) creatures.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Barter in Blood, sacrificing 2 of own 3 creatures to force opponent to sacrifice 2 of 4.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Oneirophage (4 mana flying threat that grows with card draw) to develop the board and create a blocker/threat, or cast Library Larcenist (3 mana) and still have mana for Fetid Imp's deathtouch activation. Building board presence and leveraging the card-draw synergies in hand (Rousing Read, Oneirophage, Tolarian Kraken) likely leads to a better mid-game position.

annotations.description: Sacrificing Fetid Imp (1/2 flying with deathtouch activation) when the opponent has multiple flyers (Roaming Ghostlight 3/2, Shacklegeist 2/2) that need to be blocked. Fetid Imp is one of the best defensive creatures against flying threats.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose to sacrifice Fetid Imp as one of the two creatures for Barter in Blood
annotations.betterLine: Sacrifice Liliana's Standard Bearer (3/1 vanilla at this point, ETB already used) instead of Fetid Imp, keeping the flying deathtouch blocker to deal with opponent's aerial threats

annotations.description: Blocked with Tome Anima (3/3) which will trade with the 3/1 attacker, losing a valuable unblockable threat. Could have blocked with Roaming Ghostlight instead and used Essence Flux (in hand, with U available) to save Ghostlight, get a +1/+1 counter (it's a Spirit, making it 4/3), AND trigger its ETB to bounce the opponent's only remaining creature. Instead, Tome Anima dies for nothing extra.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Liliana's Standard Bearer with Tome Anima, trading it away.
annotations.betterLine: Block with Roaming Ghostlight, then cast Essence Flux on it. Ghostlight survives as a 4/3 flyer (Spirit bonus), gets to bounce an opponent's creature with its ETB, and Tome Anima is preserved for future unblockable attacks.

annotations.description: Haiku Nature passed their postcombat main phase with zero creatures on the battlefield while facing a 5/7 World Breaker and 3/2 Roaming Ghostlight, despite having 3 mana available and multiple castable creatures. With 11 life, World Breaker alone threatens to kill them in ~2 attacks. They need to develop board presence immediately to have any chance of blocking or racing.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority with no action, ending the turn with an empty board.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Eternal Taskmaster (1B) to get a 2/3 body that can start recurring creatures from the graveyard, or Dutiful Attendant (2B) for a chump blocker that replaces itself with a graveyard creature when it dies. Either develops the board against imminent lethal pressure.
